discovery: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene: flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in moiré materials

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics (2D materials, correlated electrons)
motivation: MacDonald and Bistritzer predicted in 2011 that at a 'magic' twist angle near 1.1 degrees, the electronic bands of bilayer graphene become nearly flat, so that electron interactions dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group confirmed this with clean, gate-tuned transport experiments, reporting correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene. The twist angle turned out to be a new control parameter for quantum matter. In a single, tunable device one can now switch between insulating, superconducting, magnetic and topological phases with a gate voltage. The field of moiré materials that grew from this work has since produced orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect and, in twisted MoTe2 and rhombohedral graphene, fractional quantum anomalous Hall states at zero magnetic field. Few discoveries have opened a new materials platform so widely or so quickly. It shows well how theory and device ingenuity can work together.
